text:
Kasperi Kapanen has hit 24.05 mph this season, a top speed in the 100th percentile, and in Edmonton he has turned that into a steady role. Yardbarker ran "2 Reasons Kasperi Kapanen Has Found a Home with the Oilers," and the numbers back the move up the lineup: 18.1 minutes a night, 13 points in 25 games (7 on the power play), against 17 in 41 games last season.

His scoring rate, 1.72 points per 60, is almost exactly where we'd expect it, so the role is the change, not the talent. The goals run a bit hot: he is shooting 18.8%, above the top of our range for him, and Edmonton has scored 3.6 more goals than its chances deserved with him on.

The territory is the weak spot. The Oilers take 45.6% of the 5v5 shot attempts with him on, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 5% of forwards for creating offense last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives him one clear strength: 80% of his exits leave the zone with the puck. Our range for his season is 35 to 55 points.
